name: Lunsekimig
summary: Lunsekimig (SAR443765) is Sanofi's wholly owned bispecific nanobody blocking TSLP and IL-13, given subcutaneously. The lead Phase 3 programme is two replicate placebo-controlled studies in COPD with an eosinophilic phenotype (NCT07190209 and NCT07190222, 942 each, primary completion 2029-11-27): exacerbating (2 moderate or 1 severe in the prior year) on triple inhaled therapy, blood eosinophils of 150 cells/uL or more. Asthma is Phase 2 only and is not modelled. Price anchor: Dupixent, Sanofi's own COPD-labelled biologic, at $28,196 per Medicare Part D beneficiary in 2024 (Tezspire, the book's tozorakimab anchor, reads $29,549). Uptake anchor: the tozorakimab seed's COPD peak of 0.02039 and launch curve, which rest on Tezspire's measured share of the asthma biologic class, reused at 1.0x.

therapy_mode.source: NCT07190209, NCT07190222, and the long-term study NCT07793409 (ClinicalTrials.gov): maintenance add-on to triple inhaled therapy with exacerbation reduction as the aim
therapy_mode.note: Continuous dosing, as for Dupixent and Nucala in COPD
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table: NCT07190209/NCT07190222 primary outcome annualised rate of moderate-to-severe COPD exacerbations over a 48-week treatment period (sanofi.com/en/clinical-trials/nct07190209); maintenance add-on, chronic.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Dupixent: CMS Part D 2024, 'Dupixent (2 presentations)', $2,491,772,008 over 88,374 beneficiaries = $28,196 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator. Dupixent is Sanofi's own biologic already labelled in eosinophilic COPD (the same setting), and Sanofi is likely to price a successor near it. Case against: Dupixent's Medicare spend is mostly atopic dermatitis; the book's tozorakimab seed uses Tezspire (TSLP, the same alarmin axis) at $29,549, and Nucala (COPD-labelled since 2025, eosinophils of 150 or more, the same cut-off) reads $35,081 Part D 2024. The range is $28,196 to $35,081; the chosen value is the low end
list_price_per_patient.check: Re-ran lookup.py demand Dupixent: Part D 2024 'Dupixent (2 presentations)' $2,491,772,008 / 88,374 = $28,196 (0.028196 mm USD). Tezspire Part D 2024 $29,549 and Nucala Part D 2024 $35,081 also match the note. Nucala's US COPD approval 2025-05-22 at eosinophils from 150 cells/uL confirmed (GSK release, gsk.com/en-gb/media/press-releases/nucala-mepolizumab-approved-by-us-fda/). Comparator choice is a judgement at the low end of a $28,196-$35,081 range.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention: halving a CMS per-beneficiary figure lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices (backend/gross_to_net.py; same value in the tozorakimab seed)
gross_to_net_pct.check: Direction checked: 0.5 share off list, matches house convention and tozorakimab seed row ('share off list').

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the stock per year
discontinuation_pct.source: reused from the tozorakimab seed, which carries the respiratory biologic rate from the tilrekimig seed: Symons JM et al., J Drugs Dermatol 2025;24(10):996-1002, 55.7% of 4,562 US adults starting dupilumab still persistent at 24 months, 25.4% stopping a year at a constant rate
discontinuation_pct.note: JUDGEMENT to reuse. The measurement is Dupixent (Sanofi's own biologic) in atopic dermatitis, not COPD. Case against: older, sicker COPD patients may stop more often, including through death, which would raise the rate
discontinuation_pct.check: Symons JM et al.: 55.7% persistent at 24 months; 1 - sqrt(0.557) = 0.254. Matches the tozorakimab seed row value 0.254. Reuse from atopic dermatitis is a judgement.

forecast_start_year.source: ClinicalTrials.gov primary completion 2029-11-27 for both NCT07190209 and NCT07190222 (context file)
forecast_start_year.note: JUDGEMENT. No launch date published. Readout early 2030, a BLA by mid-2030 and a standard review put approval around mid-2031, so 2032 is the first full year. Case against: a priority review or early filing could make 2031 the first revenue year
forecast_start_year.check: PCD 2029-11-27 for both studies confirmed in context and book trials table (completion 2030-01-22). JUDGEMENT noted by the reader: the tulisokibart/duvakitug lag (PCD to first revenue year ~17 months) would give 2031 as a part-year of revenue; 2032 is the first full year. Either is defensible; kept as written.

exus_multiple.source: Dupixent, Sanofi FY2025 20-F (0001628280-26-008403), in the book's asset_revenue_regions: US EUR 11,538mm, Europe EUR 1,957mm, rest of world EUR 2,219mm. (1,957 + 2,219) / 11,538 = 0.362
exus_multiple.note: Sanofi's own respiratory and type 2 biologic, the filer's own figure. Case against: Tezspire's whole-molecule split reads lower, $458mm ex-US booked by AstraZeneca (20-F 0001104659-26-019130) over $1,478mm US booked by Amgen (10-K 0000318154-26-000010) = 0.310 in FY2025, a younger launch whose ex-US uptake may still be building
exus_multiple.check: VALUE UNCHANGED (0.3619); NOTE CORRECTED. Value and headline arithmetic hold: book asset_revenue_regions Dupilumab FY2025 US 11,538, Europe 1,957, Rest of world 2,219 (EUR mm, 0001628280-26-008403); 4,176/11,538 = 0.3619. The inconsistency is in the note's case against, corrected here: AZN's 2025 table row 'Tezspire | 458 | ... | 40 | ... | 297 | ... | 121' has 458 as AZN's World total, which is the sum 297 + 121 + 40, not a US figure (AZN books only ex-US; Amgen books US). '(297 + 121 + 40) / 458 US' is therefore 1.0 and meaningless. The like-for-like whole-molecule split is available: AZN ex-US $458mm (20-F 0001104659-26-019130) over Amgen US $1,478mm (10-K 0000318154-26-000010, book asset_revenue_regions) = 0.310, below Dupixent's 0.362.

economics_share.source: Sanofi-coded molecule (SAR443765), Sanofi lead sponsor on every listed trial (context file); no partner named in any source found
economics_share.check: SAR code is Sanofi's; book trials table lists Sanofi as lead sponsor on NCT07190209/NCT07190222; no partner found in the Sanofi 2026-04-07 phase 2 release or searches. 1.0 holds.

prevalence.source: carried by the book: epidemiology.csv, 14,200,000 (CDC BRFSS diagnosed US adults with COPD)
prevalence.note: The book fills it, so no second figure is set
prevalence.check: lookup.py pool shows epidemiology.csv carries 14,200,000 (CDC BRFSS) for this indication name; null is correct.

incidence.source: carried by the book (epidemiology.csv row, incidence blank; the tozorakimab seed sets incidence equal to prevalence)
incidence.check: epidemiology.csv incidence is blank; the tozorakimab seed carries incidence = prevalence (14,200,000) so the book holds a figure; null is correct per the brief. Caution: tozorakimab's 0.02039 peak was solved with incidence = prevalence (zero carryover); the reuse at 1.0x only reproduces the same rate if the engine fills lunsekimig's incidence the same way.

eligible_pct.source: GSK release 2025-05-22 (as cited in the book's tozorakimab eligible_pct): about 70% of US COPD patients inadequately controlled on inhaled triple therapy who continue to exacerbate have eosinophils of 150 cells/uL or more, a group of 'over a million people' (GSK Optum analysis). 1,000,000 / 14,200,000 = 0.0704. Entry criteria from NCT07190209 and NCT07190222: 2 or more moderate or 1 severe exacerbation in the prior year, triple therapy for 12 weeks or more, eosinophils 150 cells/uL or more, asthma excluded
eligible_pct.note: The GSK subgroup is exactly the Phase 3 entry pool. 'Over a million' is a floor, so the share is a lower bound. Tozorakimab's 0.1006 is the all-eosinophil version of the same figure
eligible_pct.check: GSK release 2025-05-22 (Nucala US approval) confirmed: ~70% of US COPD patients inadequately controlled on triple therapy who continue to exacerbate have eosinophils from 150 cells/uL, 'over a million people'. 1,000,000 / 14,200,000 = 0.0704, consistent with tozorakimab's 0.1006 x 0.70 = 0.0704. Trial titles confirm 'inadequately controlled COPD characterized by an eosinophilic phenotype' (NCT07190209, NCT07190222); the exact 150 cells/uL and exacerbation entry thresholds could not be opened (ClinicalTrials.gov blocked from this environment), so the pool match rests on the researcher's reading of the registry.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: reused from the tozorakimab seed: Tezspire held 16.94% of the US asthma biologic class in 2024 (13,837 Medicare beneficiaries of 81,661 across Tezspire, Nucala, Fasenra, Xolair; drug_demand), and 11.9% of severe asthma patients are on any biologic (Park et al., J Asthma Allergy 2026;19). 0.119 x 0.1694 = 2.02% of the pool, solved through the curve and 25.4% discontinuation to 0.02039
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: 1.0x, the tozorakimab multiple, so the two COPD alarmin assets in the book carry one uptake rate. Case for higher: dual TSLP/IL-13 blockade and a narrower, biomarker-selected pool in which a biologic is the natural next step. Case against: this exact pool already has Dupixent (eosinophils of 300 or more) and Nucala (150 or more), and tozorakimab and Tezspire in COPD may launch first; lunsekimig arrives around 2032 as the fourth or fifth biologic
penetration_peak_pct.check: Matches the tozorakimab seed row exactly (Tezspire 16.94% of class, 13,837/81,661; 11.9% on biologic, Park et al.; 0.119 x 0.1694 = 0.0202; solved to 0.02039). 1.0x reuse is a judgement; applied to a pool 0.70x tozorakimab's.
